guardrails: No changes to StoryPlanner, CharacterAgent, MemorySystem, ConflictResolver, WorldState core interfaces
Realizer must remain deterministic (no LLM calls)
All 186 existing tests must pass after each phase
Fallback paths must exist — never crash if substate is missing

phase_1_dialogue.name: PHASE 1 — Dialogue Guarantee & Depth
phase_1_dialogue.description: Guarantee at least one dialogue scene in SHORT mode. Increase dialogue line count per scene. Generate dialogue from character state (intentions, relationships, habits, emotional pressure, relationship sentiment). Reduce hardcoded dialogue pools by at least 30%.

Use templates like: '{goal}'s what drives me.', 'You {relationship_action} {target}.', 'I know about {discovery}.', 'This is about {goal} - nothing else.'

phase_3_scene_type_realization.name: PHASE 3 — Scene-Type Realization Diversity
phase_3_scene_type_realization.description: ACTION, DIALOGUE, REVELATION, CONFLICT, TRANSITION scenes must have unique openings, transitions, endings, and pacing. Each scene type currently shares too much structure.

changes.description: Add scene-type-specific sentence start patterns for each NarrativeMode
changes.lines: After _MODE_OUTCOMES (insert new dict before # Character voice helpers)
changes.change: Create _MODE_SENTENCE_STARTS dict mapping NarrativeMode to 10+ unique sentence opener patterns. Each mode gets distinct rhythm: CONFRONTATION starts with verbs ('He struck.', 'She turned.'), REVELATION starts with 'The', 'What', 'How', DISCOVERY starts with 'There', 'Something', TRANSITION starts with temporal markers ('As', 'When', 'Later'). These are used in paragraph composition.
changes.code_pattern:
_MODE_SENTENCE_STARTS: dict[NarrativeMode, list[str]] = {
    NarrativeMode.CONFRONTATION: [
        "He struck first.", "She did not wait.", "The blow came from nowhere.",
        "Neither moved.", "Anger drove the next move.", "Steel met steel.",
        "He lunged.", "She sidestepped.", "The impact shook them both.",
        "Blood and breath mingled.", "There was no hesitation now.",
    ],
changes.not_change: Do not modify existing mode templates. Only add new sentence start patterns used by a new paragraph composer.
changes.test_assertion: New dict has entries for all 11 NarrativeModes.

changes.description: Create a ParagraphComposer that interleaves sentence starts from _MODE_SENTENCE_STARTS with existing event text
changes.change:
Add method `_compose_paragraphs(self, events, mode) -> str` that:
1. Uses _MODE_SENTENCE_STARTS to replace the first sentence of the OPENING event 40% of the time
2. Uses scene-type-specific transition between events (action→dialogue uses different bridge than opening→reaction)
3. Uses _MODE_OUTCOMES less predictable — interleave with fresh composed closers

Currently `realize()` just joins event texts with '\n\n'. This new method adds structural variety.
changes.code_pattern:
def _compose_paragraphs(self, events: list[DramaticEvent], mode: NarrativeMode) -> str:
    paragraphs = []
    for i, event in enumerate(events):
        text = event.text
        if event.kind == EventKind.OPENING and mode in _MODE_SENTENCE_STARTS and random.random() < 0.4:
            # Replace first sentence with mode-specific start
            start = random.choice(_MODE_SENTENCE_STARTS[mode])
            text = start + ' ' + event.text
        paragraphs.append(text)
    return '

'.join(paragraphs)
changes.not_change: Keep existing event construction logic intact. ParagraphComposer only affects final assembly.
changes.test_assertion: Output contains varied sentence starts matching mode-specific patterns.

changes.description: Update realize() to use _compose_paragraphs for final assembly
changes.change: Replace the simple '\n\n'.join(paragraphs) with call to _compose_paragraphs(events, mode). The mode variable is already available from _build_event_chain. Add 'mode' as a field on DramaticRealizer instance state (self._current_mode) set during _build_event_chain.
changes.code_pattern: content = self._compose_paragraphs(events, self._current_mode) if events else ''
changes.not_change: Do not change the GeneratedScene construction or return type.
changes.test_assertion: All existing tests still pass with new paragraph composition.

phase_4_sentence_diversity.name: PHASE 4 — Sentence Diversity & Repetition Reduction
phase_4_sentence_diversity.description: Add 30+ opening patterns, 30+ transition patterns, 30+ outcome patterns. Reduce repetition_rate from 0.20 to <0.10. Increase unique_sentence_starts from 0.40 to >0.85.

changes.change: Extend each NarrativeMode's list to 15+ patterns (total 30+ across all modes). Use varied grammatical structures: prepositional phrases ('At the edge of the market...'), gerund phrases ('Walking through the rain-soaked streets...'), adverbial clauses ('While the city slept...'), direct character action ('Arjun pressed forward.'), sensory openings ('The smell of dust and old secrets hung in the air.').
changes.code_pattern:

NarrativeMode.DISCOVERY: [
    "Curiosity pulled them forward.",
    "At the edge of the known map, something waited.",
    "Walking through the ruins, he felt eyes upon him.",
    "The clue was hidden in plain sight.",
    "She ran her fingers over the worn inscription.",
    + 10 more...
]

changes.description: Add 30+ transition patterns between event types
changes.change: Create _EVENT_TRANSITIONS dict mapping (EventKind, EventKind) -> list[str]. Example: (OPENING, ACTION) -> ['Then everything changed.', 'What happened next was inevitable.', 'The moment shattered.']. Use in _compose_paragraphs to insert transition sentences between consecutive events 30% of the time.

changes.description: Add repetition detection in _compose_paragraphs: avoid same sentence start within 3 paragraphs
changes.change: In _compose_paragraphs, track the first 3 words of each paragraph. If a new paragraph would repeat the same first-3-words as any of the previous 3 paragraphs, select a different sentence start from _MODE_SENTENCE_STARTS or rephrase. This directly targets repetition_rate reduction.
changes.code_pattern:
used_starts: list[str] = []
for para in paragraphs:
    first_words = ' '.join(para.split()[:3])
    if first_words in used_starts[-3:]:
        # Replace opening with a different start
        para = self._reroll_opening(para, mode)
    used_starts.append(first_words)
changes.not_change: Do not modify the actual content of events, only how they open.
changes.test_assertion: No 3 consecutive paragraphs share same first-3-words.

phase_5_character_visibility.name: PHASE 5 — Character Visibility in Prose
phase_5_character_visibility.description: Expose OCEAN traits, dialogue habits, emotional state, relationship beliefs, drift state to alter wording, reactions, dialogue, and decisions throughout the realizer output.

changes.description: Make character OCEAN traits visible in action verb choice and adverb selection
changes.change: Increase trait_verb weight from 0.5 to 0.7 probability. Add trait-influenced location_phrase selection: brave characters choose direct paths ('through the narrow alley'), cautious characters choose indirect ('along the edge of the square'). Use OCEAN-like traits: openness (curious→exploratory verbs), conscientiousness (wise/patient→deliberate), extraversion (charismatic/brave→assertive), agreeableness (kind/gentle→helpful), neuroticism (anxious/bitter→hesitant).
changes.code_pattern: trait_verb_chance = 0.7  # CV5.1: increased from 0.5\nif random.random() < trait_verb_chance:
changes.not_change: Do not modify the trait system itself. Only increase its influence on verbs.
changes.test_assertion: Trait-appropriate verbs appear at >= 60% rate when traits match.

changes.description: Expose dialogue habits in dialogue line composition — use habit text to flavor lines
changes.change: Currently dialogue habits only modify the dialogue wrapper (prefix, suffix, tag). Expand to integrate habits into line content: if habit is 'speaks in riddles', transform line to include metaphor; if 'asks questions', append a question to the line; if 'uses sarcasm', add ironic twist. Transform is applied before voice-structure and signature phrases.
changes.code_pattern:
# CV5.2: Transform dialogue content based on habits
if voice_fp and "speaks in riddles" in voice_fp.dialogue_habits and random.random() < 0.3:
    transformed = self._riddle_transform(dialogue)
    dialogue = transformed if transformed else dialogue
changes.not_change: Do not change VoiceFingerprint dataclass or builder.
changes.test_assertion: Characters with 'speaks in riddles' habit produce metaphor-containing lines 30% of the time.

changes.description: Expose drift state in prose — desperate patterns show in action descriptions
changes.change: Currently drift already modifies action_key (line 887-890). Add visible drift markers in prose: 'desperate' drift adds urgency vocabulary ('without thinking', 'instinctively', 'recklessly'); 'erratic' adds unpredictability ('alternating between stillness and sudden movement'); 'cautious' adds hesitation markers ('paused', 'hesitated', 'measured each step'). These are injected via adverb selection and verb phrase modifiers.
changes.not_change: Do not modify BehavioralDriftTracker or drift computation.
changes.test_assertion: Drift pattern visible in action text at least 50% of the time.

changes.description: Expose relationship beliefs in character reactions and body language
changes.change: Currently reaction is pure body language. Add relationship-dependent reaction modifiers: if relationship_belief says 'enemy', reaction includes defensive posture ('stepped back', 'raised guard'); if 'ally', reaction includes openness ('leaned in', 'relaxed posture'). Use relationship belief from agent.beliefs.relationship_beliefs.
changes.not_change: Do not modify CharacterBeliefs structure.
changes.test_assertion: Reaction text changes based on relationship belief value.

changes.description: Expose emotional state in outcome composition — scene endings reflect dominant character emotion
changes.change: Currently outcome depends only on tension and resolution_goal. Add emotion-awareness: compute average emotional_pressure of involved characters and use to select from outcome sub-pools. High pressure outcomes are more desperate, low pressure more reflective.
changes.not_change: Do not change the mode-based outcome fallback logic.
changes.test_assertion: Outcome text varies based on character emotional pressure.

phase_6_memory_expression.name: PHASE 6 — Memory Expression in Prose
phase_6_memory_expression.description: Retrieved memories affect dialogue, reactions, decisions. Interpretation memories become assumptions, suspicions, expectations. No verbatim memory insertion — memories must be woven into narrative.

changes.description: Replace verbatim memory insertion in pipeline.py with narrative transformation
changes.change: Currently RAG entries are injected into agent.beliefs.discovered as 'recalled that {mem.text[:60]}' which leads to verbatim insertion. Replace with narrative transformation: store as 'remembered that {mem.text[:40]}...' or 'a {emotion} memory of {trigger_phrase}'. Use the memory's emotion_tags to determine framing (fear→'a dark memory of', joy→'a bright memory of').
changes.not_change: Do not change MemorySystem retrieval or RAGBridge.
changes.test_assertion: No 'recalled that' prefix in discovered entries. Only narrative prefixes.

changes.description: Make interpretation memories affect dialogue subtext and suspicion injection
changes.change: Currently beliefs.suspicions are injected as 'Their gaze narrowed, suspicions of {suspicion} gnawing at them.' Expand to use interpretation entries: if bp.interpretations contains entries for a character, use the interpretation_text (which says things like 'saw this as a moment of fear') to inform suspicion content. InterpretationText → suspicion key: extract emotion and build suspicion phrase like 'felt this meant danger'.
changes.code_pattern:
# ME6.2: Interpretation-informed suspicion
char_interps = [i for i in bp.interpretations if i.character == name and i.confidence > 0.6]
if char_interps and random.random() < 0.4:
    interp = random.choice(char_interps)
    suspicion_body = random.choice([
        f"A memory of {interp.emotion_impact} colored every thought.",
        f"{name} could not forget — {interp.interpretation_text[:60]}",
    ])
changes.not_change: Do not change InterpretationEngine or InterpretationStore.
changes.test_assertion: Interpretation entries appear in suspicion injection when present in blueprint.

changes.description: Use consequences to affect character action choices and urgency in prose
changes.change: In _compose_character_action, check agent's consequence history (via memory) to influence action description. If past attempts to 'confront' failed, the action verb/setup includes hesitancy. If past 'investigate' attempts succeeded, add confidence. Consequences are accessible via agent._memory.consequences_for_action(action_key) if agent._memory is set.
changes.not_change: Do not change ConsequenceEngine interface.
changes.test_assertion: Consequence-aware adverbs appear when consequence history exists.

changes.description: Relationship deltas affect relationship_phrase in action composition
changes.change: Currently relationship phrase is static per belief value. Use relationship delta recency to modulate: if a relationship recently changed (delta within last chapter), add additional reaction text reflecting uncertainty or adjustment. Access via agent._memory.recent_relationship_changes(agent.name).
changes.not_change: Do not modify RelationshipDeltaTracker.
changes.test_assertion: Recent relationship changes produce uncertainty phrases in action text.

changes.description: No verbatim memory insertion — ensure _compose_memory_callback never copies raw memory text
changes.change: Currently memory callback templates use `mem_text = mem.text[:60]` directly inserted. Replace with transformation: extract key nouns from mem_text, build new sentence like 'The memory of {key_nouns} resurfaced.' or '{character} could still feel the weight of what happened.' Never use `mem.text` verbatim — always transform through templates.
changes.code_pattern:
# ME6.5: No verbatim memory — extract and transform
mem_text = mem.text[:60]
# Extract key 2-3 nouns for narrative transformation
words = [w for w in mem_text.split() if w[0].isupper() or w in _SIGNIFICANT_NOUNS]
key_elements = ' '.join(words[:3]) if words else mem_text.split()[:2]
templates = [
    f"The memory of {key_elements} flickered through their mind.",
    f"{key_elements} — the thought came unbidden, sharp and clear.",
    f"They could still feel the echo of that moment. {key_elements} had changed everything.",
]
changes.not_change: Do not modify emotion-tag-based templates (they already use transformation).
changes.test_assertion: No verbatim memory text in callback output. Every callback is a rephrasing.

risk_assessment.summary: Primary risks are: (1) dialogue changes may break HWSE pipeline if scene structure changes too much, (2) memory expression changes may alter memory callback behavior, (3) paragraph composer may change well-formedness of existing test assertions.

mitigations.hwse_breakage: All changes to build_*_scene methods preserve the event structure (opening, actions, complications, outcome). Only adding events, never removing. HWSE operates on GeneratedScene after realizer.realize(), so event-level changes don't affect it.
mitigations.test_regression: Existing tests check for word_count > 5 and scene_type matching. These are preserved. New events add words → word_count increases but remains > 5. Scene_type comes from blueprint, unchanged.
mitigations.memory_verbatim_removal: The verbatim removal in ME6.5 only affects _compose_memory_callback output format. All existing tests pass because they check for scene existence, not callback text content.
